newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Merrill Lynch acquires 7.7 pct of Liraz.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch acquires 7.7 pct of Liraz.

text.p: Merrill Lynch has acquired 7.7 percent of Israel's Liraz Systems Ltd, a software house, for $3.6 million from the company's controlling shareholder, a Merrill Lynch spokesman in London said on Thursday.

He said Merrill had acquired 400,000 shares at 32.13 shekels, equal to a discount of 9.5 percent on Liraz's Tel Aviv-traded share price at the time of the transaction. The seller was Liraz's chief executive officer Arie Kilman.
Liraz shares fell one percent to 37.25 shekels on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange on Thursday.
In addition, Kilman sold another 100,000 shares for the same price to IBI, the Israeli brokerage that conducted the Merrill Lynch transaction, sources said.

It was the third transaction of this kind in Israel for Merrill Lynch. In June it acquired 19 percent of drug manufacturer Agis Industries Ltd for $58.6 million and in February acquired $9.25 million in warrants in software house Formula Systems Ltd.
The Merrill Lynch spokesman declined to comment on what the company would be doing with the shares.
The Agis shares were a block trade transferred to customers and the Formula warrants were to be used as the basis for an offering of American depositary receipts (ADRs) in the United States.
Yossi Shemesh, Liraz's finance director, said he did not know why Merrill had taken the stake but said Liraz had no immediate plans to float ADRs in the U.S.
"The sale opens the possibility of offerings ADRs, but we have no immediate plans," he told Reuters.
Liraz has sales of $23 million and controls Nasdaq-traded Level 8 systems Inc, a provider of IBM mainframe software middleware services.
